explanations.explanation: Mark 6:1 says Jesus "…came to His hometown, accompanied by His disciples." So He isn't just passing through somewhere new. He's heading to His own hometown. Home is a big deal, friend, and I think this trip is going to be a big one.

Jerusalem is a big name, so I get why it jumped out. But the text never sends Jesus there in this passage. Mark 6:1 says He came to His hometown, with His disciples right beside Him. Keep your eyes on home, friend.
Bethany is a nice guess, but this passage never mentions it. Mark 6:1 tells us Jesus went on from there and came to His hometown. His disciples came along too. Home is the stop on this map, baker.

Mark 6:2 says "…many who heard Him were astonished." They were stunned enough to start asking out loud where all this came from. I bet that synagogue got LOUD with questions. Astonished is the word, baker, and it's a big one.

Bored folks don't ask question after question about what they just heard. The text says many who heard Him were astonished. People who are bored don't ask "What is this wisdom He has been given?" They ask where the door is, friend.

Frightened is a fair guess, but the text doesn't say it. Mark 6:2 says "…many who heard Him were astonished." Think of how you feel when someone you thought you had figured out does something that makes you say, "Wait, WHAT?" That's the crowd here. Astonished is the word, baker.
They really do ask it. Mark 6:2 has them wondering, "And how can He perform such miracles?" They're puzzling over how Jesus can do such things. Wisdom AND miracles, both on the table, friend.

The text says otherwise. In Mark 6:2 the crowd asks, "And how can He perform such miracles?" That question sits right next to their questions about His wisdom. So the miracles are on their minds too, baker.

They say, "Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary…" (Mark 6:3). Notice they don't even need to look Him up. They knew His trade before they finished the sentence. That's what a hometown does to you, friend. Everybody already has your job title memorized.
Close to a good guess, but that isn't the word in the text. In Mark 6:3 the hometown crowd says, "Isn’t this the carpenter…" That's the job they know Him by. Carpenter, baker.

Shepherd isn't the word the crowd uses here. Mark 6:3 has them asking, "Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary…" That's what they call Him in that synagogue. They know His work, and they say it plain.

Mark 6:3 says, "And they took offense at Him." They started out astonished and ended up offended, and that's a quick turn, friend. The text doesn't tell us exactly why. It just tells us that's where the crowd lands.

explanations.answer: They ask Him to stay longer
explanations.explanation: No invitation to stay shows up in this passage. Mark 6:2 says many were astonished and asked their questions, and then Mark 6:3 says "…they took offense at Him." After that, Jesus is the one who speaks next. Nobody asks Him to stay, baker.

explanations.answer: They follow Him to the next town
explanations.explanation: This passage never says the crowd follows Him anywhere. Mark 6:3 says "…they took offense at Him." Later, in verse 6, Jesus goes around from village to village teaching the people. The text doesn't mention the hometown crowd tagging along, friend.

That's a big "everywhere," friend, and Jesus doesn't say it. In Mark 6:4 He says, "Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor." He names three things: his hometown, his relatives and his own household. Words like "only" matter.

Jesus is much more specific than "everywhere." Mark 6:4 says, "Only in his hometown, among his relatives, and in his own household is a prophet without honor." He names his hometown, his relatives and his own household, and the word "only" matters. Good catch, baker.

explanations.answer: He lays hands on a few sick people and heals them
explanations.explanation: Mark 6:5 says Jesus "…could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them." So there is healing, just a few people's worth. It's a small number next to the crowd that took offense. I think those few went home glad, baker.

explanations.answer: He drives demons out of a man in town
explanations.explanation: Demons don't show up in this passage. Mark 6:5 says the one exception was that He laid His hands on a few of the sick and healed them. Stick to that verse, friend, and you're in good shape.

explanations.answer: He calms a storm out on the nearby lake
explanations.explanation: No storm and no lake in this passage, baker. Mark 6:5 says He "…could not perform any miracles there, except to lay His hands on a few of the sick and heal them." The scene stays in town.

Mark 6:6 says, "And He was amazed at their unbelief." Jesus Himself is amazed, and that's the word the text gives us. Earlier in the passage the crowd was the one astonished, so now the amazement goes the other direction. Quite a switch, friend.

Mark 6:6 says Jesus was amazed at their unbelief, the opposite of faith. This crowd heard Him teach, asked about His wisdom and miracles, and still took offense. It's a different word from the one you picked, baker.
Kindness isn't the word here. Mark 6:6 says, "And He was amazed at their unbelief." This crowd has just taken offense at Jesus, so a kind reception isn't what the text shows. Unbelief is the word.

explanations.answer: He goes from village to village teaching
explanations.explanation: Mark 6:6 says, "And He went around from village to village, teaching the people." The hometown said no, and Jesus keeps right on teaching. He doesn't stop, friend. He just moves on to the next place.

explanations.answer: He goes up a mountain alone to pray
explanations.explanation: That's not what this verse says, baker. Mark 6:6 says Jesus "…went around from village to village, teaching the people." No mountain and no going off alone here. He keeps teaching.

explanations.answer: He sails back across the sea to rest
explanations.explanation: No sea and no rest in this passage. Mark 6:6 says Jesus went around from village to village, teaching the people. He keeps right on with the work, friend.
